coverage_exempt.reason: Original 0x4db6e0 can return zero only after realloc failure; 0x4db70b/0x4db77f copies zero into EBP and 0x4db788 calls 0x4dc680, whose first instruction reads [EBP+4]. The unchanged original faults before returning to this recovery block.

The original first lookup either begins inside signed table bounds or successful 0x4db6e0 updates lower/upper bounds at 0x4db757/0x4db7dc to include the unchanged index. No intervening call or bounds write occurs before the second lookup; its out-of-range path cannot execute.

The second lookup cannot be out of range after the first successful lookup: original 0x4db6e0 expands bounds to include the same index, and no intervening call or bounds write occurs. Its failure recovery is therefore unreachable; additionally realloc failure faults in 0x4dc680 before return.

equivalent_mutants.reason: The swapped store/call are wholly inside the first table-growth failure recovery block (original 0x406f45..0x406f73). Original 0x4db6e0 reaches a zero return only following failed realloc: 0x4db70b or 0x4db77f sets EBP=0, then 0x4db788 calls 0x4dc680, whose first instruction reads [EBP+4] and faults. Thus the unchanged original cannot return into this block on any valid ordinary entry; neither ordering executes. Checked against original disassembly 0x4db6e0 and 0x4dc680, not inferred from surviving tests.
